Cara Mengatasi Rasa Gatal Di Selangkangan

Ingredients:

  • 2 large leeks
  • 2 large carrots
  • 2 large russet potatoes
  • 1lbs ground lamb
  • 1 small can of tomato paste
  • Chicken stock
  • Worcestershire sauce
  • Flour
  • Frozen peas
  • Butter
  • Sour Cream
  • Whole Milk
  • 1 egg

Directions:

  • Preheat oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit.

  • Prep vegetables. Clean and chop leeks. Peel and chop carrots. Peel and cube potatoes.

  • Add potatoes to pot of cold, salted water. Bring to boil then cook until soft, about 15 minutes.

  • While potatoes are boiling, add oil to a large, deep pan and bring to medium high heat. Add leeks and carrots, sautee until soft. Season to taste. (I use salt, pepper, garlic powder, and a small dash of cayenne.)

  • When leeks and carrots are soft, add ground lamb and cook until the meat is cooked through.

  • Add flour to meat and coat well. (I use 4 to 5 tablespoons. It depends how thick you want your filling to be.)

  • Add tomato paste and mix everything together.

  • Add chicken stock, anywhere between 1 and 2 cups, depending on the size of the leeks and carrots you used. You want your own to be soupy, but to cook down until it's thick.

  • Add Worcestershire sauce. A lot. When you think you've added a little too much, splash some more on there. I do this step by gut feeling and have never measured how much I use, but I use a lot. Enough to darken the filling a lot.

  • When the potatoes are finished, drain and mash. Add a little butter, sour cream, whole milk, and 1 egg yolk and mix well.

  • Add frozen peas to filling, enough so that there is an equal amount of leeks, carrots, and peas. Mix together.

  • Add filling to a baking dish (I use a Pyrex loaf pan. A deeper, narrower dish is better than a shallow, wide one.) And cover with mashed potatoes.

  • Bake until potatoes are browned.

Note: This is a recipe I've developed over the years and I've never tried writing it down. Sorry if I was unconventional in the order I listed my ingredients list or if my directions weren't how recipes are usually formatted.

This recipe is very flexible. You don't really need the sour cream for the potatoes, for example, and you can use any type of milk rather than whole milk. Within reason. Don't use chocolate milk and come crying to me that you don't like the taste. Add corn if you want. Or, if you're frugal, make it a cottage pie and use ground beef and onions instead of ground lamb and leeks. It will still taste great.

Lastly, I occasionally make this with mashed rutabaga instead of mashed potatoes. If you're interested, then just peel large rutabaga, cut into cubes, add to cold, salted water, then bring to a boil and cook until soft - about 45 minutes. Drain, add black pepper to taste, and mash. No egg.
